_note: A ceiling, not a target. Every number below was COUNTED by the counters in tests/guardrails/motion-parity.test.ts, on the integrated motion/p4-token-foundation branch: the token layer plus the three wrappers plus the byte-identical migrations that landed with them (a 0.4/0.86 sheet spring onto Settle; the web's press and calendar-paging curves onto var(--tday-ease-gesture), which is the same (0.2,0.8,0.2,1) they spelled out). They are NOT reproducible at 4c941b1c, which predates the wrappers: counted there, ios.spring is 110 and web.rawCubicBezier is 11, and three of the paths this file excludes do not exist yet. The branch is the unit these numbers belong to, not the commit. The assertion is actual <= budget: this file does not ask anyone to migrate, it asks that nobody add. Lower a number whenever a migration PR takes sites off it; raise one only alongside a call-site comment arguing why that value is deliberately not a token, the way MotionTokens.kt requires.
_measuredBy: tday-web/tests/guardrails/motion-parity.test.ts — the COUNTERS table. The regexes live there rather than here because a count is only meaningful as the output of a rule, and a fixture cannot hold the rule.

_excluded._why: Each path below is a file whose entire job is to hold these numbers once. Counting them would raise every budget by the size of the token layer on the day it landed, and every later migration would move a literal from a counted file to an excluded one for no net change — a ratchet that measures nothing. What is counted is what has NOT been migrated yet.
_excluded.comments: Comment text is stripped before counting, in every language. This PR's own call-site comments argue in place for why a value is NOT a token and quote the numbers while doing it — one of them contains a literal 'response: 0.28,' inside a doc comment. Counting those would let an argument for leaving a value alone raise the budget it is arguing about.
_excluded.notCountedOnPurpose: The ~159 bare Tailwind transition-* utilities in tday-web/src. They ride --default-transition-duration, which is an un-overridden 150ms and therefore already exactly the Quick rung. They are on the vocabulary for free; rebinding that default would be a visible change to all of them.

android._tween: durationMillis = <n>, or tween(<n>. 35 when the token layer landed; one came off in Phase 6 when the root dock's tab tint stopped crossfading on a hand-written 180 and joined the create button and the feed body under them on the Quick rung, and five more when the staged check-off moved onto the rungs — the three rows' fades onto Change, the Completed screen's title colour onto Emphasis when it stopped being the one Android row still on 180/180, plus one 320 that was computed every frame and drawn by nobody.
android._spring: dampingRatio = <n> or stiffness = <n>, written out. Compose's Spring.StiffnessMediumLow and friends are library defaults rather than decisions — the audit found Android's 400 to be exactly that — so they are not counted and moving onto one is not progress.
android._pressScale: a scale literal in [0.90, 1.0) on a line that also says scale or press. This catches a few enter-scales alongside the press ones (EnterStartScale = 0.92f); they are the same family and the same PRs will touch them, so the over-count is honest rather than convenient. 31 when the ratchet landed, and unmoved until Phase 9's 9b2: the two hero circle buttons — the root feed's search/close pair and the list header's back chevron — each computed a 0.93 of their own from a bare `if (pressed)` inside `graphicsLayer`, so the squash arrived in one frame and left in one under a ripple that took its own time. Both are on `Modifier.tdayPressable` at `PressScales.Bar` now, which is a retune as well as a migration: 0.94, because these are bar buttons and the FAB keeps 0.93. Six more came off in 9b3 and one went back on. The scheduled feed's entire parallel FAB went out with the `showCreateTaskButton` flag — a Scaffold slot, its own private `CreateTaskButton`, and a `PressableIconButton` beside it with no caller anywhere in the tree — and those were two of the 0.93s; the one screen that still drew from that slot, the locked onboarding backdrop, was given a plain `RootCreateTaskButton` instead, so the corner keeps its button and the press behind it is the token one; the today card and the list rows under it stopped inventing 0.97 and 0.98 and named `Card` and `Row`; and the root dock's selector and tab content did the same, the selector's 0.985 being `Row` to the byte. The one that went back on is `TdayPress.FabScale`, which is that same 0.93 written once for the two Android FABs that were each spelling it out. It is a literal in a counted file on purpose: the alternative is a fourth generated token in all three clients, and web's FAB is 0.95. Eight more in 9b1, the leaf-screen sweep: the round bar button that Guide, Calendar, Completed, Latest release and Settings had each copied for themselves, the calendar's accent "Today" pill beside one of them, the sheet chrome's toolbar action and the members sheet's full-width action row. Seven of the eight wrote 0.93 — a depth nothing on Android ever argued for, against `PressScales.Bar`'s 0.94, which iOS did argue, at `TaskFloatingActionButton.swift:162-166` — so those seven are a retune of a hundredth as well as a migration; the eighth was already 0.97 to the byte and merely stopped spelling `Card` out. Nothing was added back: the sheet action's three-way elevation `when` stays where it is, because `cardElevation` has two states and it needs three, and its 1 dp sink and its `enabled` gate are arguments to the modifier rather than literals of its own. Eight more in 9b4, the feed surfaces, and the migration ends there. `TodoListScreen`'s list FAB (the second of the two 0.93s `TdayPress.FabScale` was written for), its Today header button, its Floater list row, and the two list-settings tiles; the category card; and the segmented slider's selector and segment content. Three of those handed an elevation leg back to `CardDefaults.cardElevation` — an `animateDpAsState` fed into `defaultElevation` AND `pressedElevation` is a way of animating an elevation behind Material's back, and the pair it wants is just the two ends. The two slider scales did NOT move onto the modifier and are the only two here that did not: the selector is not a surface reading its own press but a floating pill whose interaction source belongs to an option below it, and both share a spring with the offset that slides it, which the shared modifier deliberately cannot take. They name the token and keep the spring; the selector's 0.985 was `PressScales.Row` to the byte and the segment content moved a half-hundredth onto it so the label and the pill under it press together. THE CEILING AND THE SURVIVORS ARE NOW THE SAME EIGHT, which is what makes a ninth always new: `TaskSwipeActionButton.kt:49` and `CalendarScreen.kt:2978`, each one factor of a composed transform and argued in place (`docs/motion.md`'s "Deliberate non-tokens" table, :547); `TdaySegmentedSlider.kt:205`, a halo growing INTO view rather than a surface sinking; `TdayEmptyState.kt:380`'s `EnterStartScale`, an enter; `TdayHeroTitleHeader.kt:141`'s `DockedTitleScaleFrom`, a scroll-driven dock; `RootFeedDock.kt:500` and `:501`, the tab's own 0.94→1 expansion multiplied by the press token beside it; and `TdayPressable.kt:82`'s `FabScale`, the one press depth in the tree that is still a literal, on purpose and argued where it is written. None of those eight is a press site inventing a depth, so the next line this counter sees will be — the argument `web.rawCubicBezier` already makes for itself two keys down.

ios._spring: response: <n> and dampingFraction: <n>, counted separately — so one hand-written .spring() costs two. Nineteen of these pairs are the exact 0.28/0.86 that the Snappy token was re-anchored on. 108 after the token layer landed; four came off in Phase 7's two feed cuts, where the today block and the calendar's day list each stopped timing their rows against a 0.34/0.9 spring nothing else in the repo shared and joined TdayFeedItemMotion. Two more in Phase 8's 35b: the root dock's collapse/expand swap was spelling out 0.34/0.82, which is the Gesture spring exactly — a control carrying on after a finger has let go — so naming the token cost no pixels and is what put a Reduce Motion gate beside it. Four more in Phase 8's 48, where the swipe cleanup took SwipeRevealHintModifier out: its 0.26/0.78 nudge and 0.38/0.68 return are the same two springs TodoTrailingSwipeActionsModifier.revealHint() writes, and the modifier holding the copy had had no caller since the trailing swipe absorbed the hint.
ios._easeDuration: duration: <n> — .easeInOut(duration:), .easeOut(duration:), .snappy(duration:) and the static lets that hold them. Note this is the grep that CANNOT see the generated file's own durations, which are 'static let quick: TimeInterval = 0.15' with no duration: anywhere on the line, and that it equally cannot see TdayMotion.standard(duration: TdayMotion.Durations.change), which is what a migrated site looks like. 56 when the token layer landed; one came off in Phase 6 when the onboarding backdrop stopped timing its blur with a 0.22 of its own, and twenty-two more when the four screens that stage a check-off put its beats on the rungs, and five more when the feed-item split landed: the 0.22 the timeline's travel ran on, the 0.22 the view model wrapped a remote cache change in, and the Completed screen's 0.24/0.16/0.1 trio, all of which are now TdayFeedItemMotion. One more in Phase 8's 35a repair: the root snackbar's .snappy(duration: 0.3) is TdayMotion.snappy, which is both the token that hand-written spring was approximating and the one .animation in AppRootView that Reduce Motion could not switch off — the literal paid for a gate rather than a retiming.

web._durationUtility: Tailwind duration-<n> utilities. Most are duration-200, which is already the Enter rung numerically — they are counted anyway, because a utility that happens to equal a token is not the same thing as a site that names one. 73 when the token layer landed; three came off in Phase 6 when the hero header's two sibling controls moved onto duration-quick and its title stopped declaring a transition the rAF was overwriting, and twelve more when the five rows that play the check-off put the strike's colour transition on duration-emphasis and the checkbox's pop on duration-quick. Eleven more in Phase 9's 41a, where web's four overlay systems stopped each timing themselves: the sheet's 500-in/300-out became Emphasis-in/Enter-out (a side panel travelling its own width is geometry, and an exit is never longer than the enter it undoes), and the three centred systems stopped timing themselves too: Modal and the centred selector spell Enter in and Quick out instead of 200/200 and 300/200, while the dialog's one bare duration-200 — the only rung it declares, covering both directions — became one bare duration-enter. Modal's MODAL_EXIT_MS moved with its own class in the same edit: that constant is read twice on purpose, so a rung named on only one side would half-play the exit.
web._rawCubicBezier: cubic-bezier( written out at a call site. All three survivors are deliberate orphans with no token and no second site: globals.css (0.3,0,0.4,1), RootDock.tsx (0.25,1,0.5,1), AnimatedHeight.tsx (0.22,0.61,0.36,1), the wizard's own height curve promoted with the primitive that now holds it. Cited by curve and not by line: a line number recorded in a fixture is stale the moment anything above it moves, and one of these three moved twice while this PR was being written. With the Gesture curve named, those three orphans ARE the count — the ceiling and the list are the same three sites, so a fourth is always new.
web._cssMsLiteral: a bare <n>ms in CSS or in an inline style string. 19 when the token layer landed; two came off in Phase 5, one of them the inline `height 280ms` the onboarding wizard animated with, which moved to the Emphasis rung when `AnimatedHeight` became a primitive; four more in Phase 6 — `.task-strike`'s own 320ms, and the three `opacity 300ms ease` strings the rows that were not on `taskCompletionTiming` each wrote out for themselves. Two more in Phase 7, when the calendar's two paging slides stopped running on a hand-written 260 and joined the height box under them on Emphasis — the rung both halves of a page turn answer to, the slide moving the grid and the box resizing the card around it. One more when the calendar row's highlight ring joined the tint beside it on the Quick rung. Five more in Phase 7's swipe unit, which is the retiming that note was waiting for: the three rows' `transform 220ms ease` and the two surviving `background-color 150ms ease` beside them are one string in `swipeGesture.ts` now, and a released row settles on Quick going home and Emphasis going open — the rungs the calendar's own pager already answers a refused swipe and a turned page with. Two more in Phase 7's press-cascade unit, which had to name both numbers to argue about them: the blanket press rule's 180 is Quick now — the rung for the app answering a finger, and the un-overridden 150 every bare `transition-*` already rides, so a shadcn Button and a plain one no longer press at two different lengths — and the ripple's 340 is Emphasis, which is the rung a change of size answers to and is that band's own value to within a frame. One more in Phase 7's route hand-over, where the fade a screen arrives on stopped being a hand-written 140 and became `Enter` — the rung for a thing arriving that has no reason to be another length. The 140 was an argument against the LONG end (not `Scene`, not Android's 360) and that half of it is restated at the call site; what it could not defend was 140 itself, which named no rung. The ceiling holds at 2 through Phase 8's reduced-motion floor, which retired one literal to pay for the one it added: `.tday-empty-enter`'s hand-written 520 is `var(--tday-duration-scene)` now — the Scene rung's own and only site, which had simply never been migrated — and the 1ms the blanket floor pins every animation to took its place. That 1ms is the one value here that argues for itself rather than for a rung: zero is what the eye wants, and a zero-length animation's `animationend` is not something every engine agrees to fire, which is the whole reason the floor floors instead of switching motion off.
